title: Give an informal argument for the angle-angle criterion for similar triangles

sections.skill: Give an informal argument for the angle-angle criterion for similar triangles

questions.skill: Give an informal argument for the angle-angle criterion for similar triangles
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has angles of 40° at A and 75° at B. Triangle DEF has angles of 40° at D and 75° at E, and DE = 2 · AB. Explain, using a dilation and rigid motions, why the triangles are similar.
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangle ABC has angles of 40° at A and 75° at B. Triangle DEF has angles of 40° at D and 75° at E, and DE = 2 · AB.
Explain, using a dilation and rigid motions, why the triangles are similar.
questions.required_method: Dilate ABC by a scale factor of 2, so the image of AB has the same length as DE. Rigid motions then move that image onto DE, with the third vertex on the same side as F. The 40° and 75° angles make the other two sides lie along rays DF and EF, which meet at only one point, so the third vertex lands on F. A dilation followed by rigid motions maps ABC onto DEF.

questions.skill: Give an informal argument for the angle-angle criterion for similar triangles
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Explain why two triangles with two pairs of equal angles must also have the third pair of angles equal.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why two triangles with two pairs of equal angles must also have the third pair of angles equal.
questions.required_method: In each triangle the three angles add to 180°, so each third angle equals 180° minus the same two measures. The third angles are equal.

questions.skill: Give an informal argument for the angle-angle criterion for similar triangles
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: Use a ruler and a protractor to draw two triangles of different sizes that each have angles of 50° and 60°. Measure their sides, and compare the ratios of corresponding sides.
questions.prompt_markup: Use a ruler and a protractor to draw two triangles of different sizes that each have angles of 50° and 60°. Measure their sides, and compare the ratios of corresponding sides.
questions.correct_answer: The ratios of corresponding sides are all about the same (equal up to measuring error), so the triangles are similar.
questions.drawing_answer: Two triangles of different sizes, each with angles of 50°, 60°, and 70°
questions.grading_note: Grade the two drawings and the ratios computed from the student's own measurements; there is no preset size.

questions.skill: Prove the triangle proportionality theorem with similar triangles
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC, and DE is parallel to BC. Prove that AD ÷ AB = AE ÷ AC. Give a reason for each step.
questions.prompt_markup:
In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC, and DE is parallel to BC.
Prove that AD ÷ AB = AE ÷ AC. Give a reason for each step.
questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Other valid orders are accepted. A conclusion without reasons is not full credit. Example: angle ADE = angle ABC (corresponding angles, DE ∥ BC); angle A is shared; so triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC (AA), and corresponding sides are proportional: AD ÷ AB = AE ÷ AC.

questions.skill: Explain why trigonometric ratios depend only on the angle (similar right triangles)
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Two right triangles each have a 35° angle. Explain why the ratio (leg opposite 35°) ÷ (hypotenuse) is the same in both.
questions.prompt_markup:
Two right triangles each have a 35° angle.
Explain why the ratio (leg opposite 35°) ÷ (hypotenuse) is the same in both.
questions.correct_answer: Both triangles have a 90° angle and a 35° angle, so they are similar by AA, and corresponding sides of similar triangles have equal ratios.
